disclaimer: Public-source research only. Priority is a research ranking, not a claim that a company is for sale or that any owner wants to exit.

companies.name: Schelter Heating and Air
companies.why: Founder Ron Schelter states he founded the family-owned company in 1997. The company has a long local operating history and a comparatively simple digital footprint, while the public site also lists Matt Schelter as a contact. That combination creates a potentially interesting owner-dependence / succession diligence case without assuming an exit.
companies.counter: A family member is visibly involved, so succession may already be developing internally.
companies.next: Confirm Georgia entity ownership and license holder; map Ron vs. Matt responsibilities; estimate technician count and service fleet; verify maintenance-plan/customer-base depth; then make low-pressure owner-to-owner outreach focused on legacy and continuity.

companies.name: Allen Norris HVAC, LLC
companies.why: BBB reports the business started in 2008 and identifies Allen Norris as president. It is A+ rated and offers residential and commercial HVAC, but has a relatively modest public digital surface compared with scaled regional brands.
companies.counter: Public sources do not establish size, recurring revenue, or whether the company is meaningfully owner-dependent.
companies.next: Verify Secretary of State ownership, license, fleet/team size, Google review velocity, maintenance agreements and commercial mix; prioritize a confidential introductory call only after confirming scale.

companies.name: McBroom Heating and Air Conditioning, Inc.
companies.why: BBB reports 23 years in business and identifies Houston McBroom as owner. The company appears substantially less digitally scaled than large North Atlanta competitors, which is consistent with the hidden-value thesis.
companies.counter: Public evidence on employees, recurring service agreements and current revenue mix is sparse.
companies.next: Verify active license/entity; identify service territory, review count, trucks/technicians, commercial exposure and maintenance base; if still a small owner-led platform, place it near the top of direct outreach.

companies.name: Pruitt Heating & Air, Inc.
companies.thesis: Long-duration family business with service depth
companies.why: The company says it has served customers since 1978, is family owned and operated, serves homes and businesses, and emphasizes long-term customer relationships. That is a strong quality/recurring-service profile.
companies.counter: Its digital presence and Trane positioning are more mature than a truly invisible operator; ownership/management succession is not clear from current public sources.
companies.next: Identify current shareholders and family management; estimate maintenance-plan penetration and commercial share; verify whether management runs independently of ownership before outreach.

companies.name: Service First HVAC, Inc.
companies.why: Founded in 1997, family- and veteran-owned, with a strong commercial HVAC focus. Public team information shows founder John Krauss and newer owner Tim Krauss, who rose internally from apprentice to installation manager and ownership. This is a credible succession story and potentially a durable platform.
companies.counter: The presence of a newer owner means transition may already be successfully underway, reducing urgency as an acquisition target.
companies.next: Map ownership percentages and decision rights between John and Tim; determine commercial maintenance-contract concentration, customer concentration and management depth; outreach should position a partnership/recapitalization option rather than assume a full sale.

companies.name: Cool-Tech HVAC, Inc.
companies.thesis: Established multi-family operator with real operating infrastructure
companies.why: Family-owned, with roots going to 2003; public information describes 30+ employees, a fleet, warehouse, sheet-metal shop, residential and commercial work, and multiple family members involved. That is materially stronger infrastructure than a small owner-operator.
companies.counter: Multiple family members and operating managers may mean succession is already institutionalized; acquisition affordability may also be lower.
companies.next: Confirm current ownership between the Slayden family members, recurring maintenance/commercial mix, EBITDA scale and second-line management. Treat as a platform-quality target, not a distressed or unsophisticated seller.

companies.name: Hansard Heating & Cooling
companies.why: Family-owned, serving North Georgia and Metro Atlanta since 2002, with both residential and small-commercial HVAC. It has enough history to suggest a meaningful installed customer base but is not presented like a large consolidator-style platform.
companies.counter: Public ownership and management depth are not clearly disclosed, so the owner-dependence thesis still needs proof.
companies.next: Identify owners/license holder, team and truck count, review density, maintenance memberships and commercial recurring revenue; then determine whether an owner-led continuity conversation is warranted.

companies.name: Suwanee Mechanical
companies.why: The company states it is family owned with roughly 20 years of operating history and serves both residential and commercial customers. Its public positioning remains relatively straightforward rather than heavily institutionalized.
companies.counter: The current website has been modernized, and public data does not identify ownership or team size.
companies.next: Resolve legal entity and owner names, license holder, technician count, commercial-maintenance book and geography; score higher only if customer relationships and operations remain concentrated around the owner.

companies.name: ACR Heating & Air
companies.why: ACR states it has served North Metro Atlanta and North Georgia since 1997. Its messaging emphasizes personal service, fixed pricing and custom work rather than a multi-brand home-services rollup model.
companies.counter: Public ownership, scale and management structure are not sufficiently visible from the current source set.
companies.next: Identify owners and entity history, quantify service area/reviews/fleet, look for maintenance membership and commercial work, and verify there is no sponsor/franchise ownership before direct outreach.

companies.name: H & H Mechanical
companies.why: Founded in 1983 and still described as family owned/local, with HVAC, plumbing, commercial capabilities, BBB A+ positioning and a strong long operating history.
companies.counter: The company has professionalized operations and a director of operations, suggesting lower owner dependency and higher valuation. It is also outside the tightest North Atlanta search radius.
companies.next: Determine current shareholders after founders Paul Harris and Billy Honea, management autonomy, service-agreement base and revenue by HVAC vs plumbing. Consider as a larger platform/benchmark rather than first-wave outreach.

companies.name: Empire Heating & Air Conditioning
companies.why: Founded by Martin and Gila Hoover in 1985. The current team page identifies Martin as president plus sales, operations, service and production managers and a Hoover family CFO, showing both family continuity and a real management structure.
companies.counter: That management depth reduces key-person risk and makes the company less 'hidden' than the ideal target.
companies.next: Map family ownership and Mason Hoover's role, quantify recurring maintenance and branch economics, and determine whether the owners seek liquidity/partner capital rather than assuming succession pressure.

companies.name: Reliance Heating and Air Conditioning
companies.why: BBB says Reliance has operated since 1968, is family owned and operated, and identifies Michael Bilbrey as president and Matt Bilbrey as vice president. It provides commercial HVAC, planned maintenance and new-construction HVAC in addition to residential work.
companies.counter: Visible family management suggests succession already exists; its depth and sophistication reduce the hidden-value gap.
companies.next: Treat as a high-quality platform benchmark. Verify ownership percentages, locations, commercial contract base and whether management is independent; pursue only if valuation/owner objectives fit.

companies.name: Cunningham Associates
companies.why: Locally managed/operated since 2005 with owner involvement, NATE/EPA technicians and recurring maintenance positioning. LinkedIn describes 11-50 employees and employee ownership/frontline owner involvement.
companies.counter: Employee ownership and professional digital/marketing systems can materially complicate a traditional owner-buyout thesis.
companies.next: Verify ESOP/employee-ownership structure and cap table before doing anything else. If employee-owned, decide whether the transaction structure is even compatible with your acquisition strategy.

companies.name: Neese Heating & Air Conditioning
companies.thesis: Strong established company with visible management continuity
companies.why: BBB reports operations since 1992 and identifies Jordan Neese as general manager; another BBB profile identifies Dewey Neese Jr. as owner and Morgan Neese. The company offers service agreements plus HVAC and plumbing.
companies.counter: Multiple Neese family members and a general manager indicate an active succession/management structure, while a strong digital/review footprint reduces the hidden-value gap.
companies.next: Map ownership and Jordan/Morgan/Dewey responsibilities; use as a platform-quality candidate only if owners want liquidity—not as a presumed succession problem.

companies.name: Air Pro Heating & Air
companies.thesis: Established family operator, but digitally mature
companies.why: The company states it is family owned and has provided HVAC service for over 30 years, with NATE-certified technicians and online booking/financing.
companies.counter: Modern digital infrastructure and mature operating systems narrow the hidden-value gap; current ownership details are not obvious from the public pages reviewed.
companies.next: Verify shareholders, management bench, service-plan base and scale. Keep on the list, but below more owner-concentrated/local candidates.

companies.name: Zone Heating & Air
companies.why: Family owned for 25+ years, multiple offices, thousands of five-star reviews, NATE technicians and mature guarantees/marketing. It has clear recurring maintenance and multi-location operating capability.
companies.counter: Exactly because it is scaled and sophisticated, it is not a hidden-value candidate and likely commands a premium multiple.
companies.next: Use it as a market benchmark for what a scaled independent platform looks like. Only pursue if your strategy expands to larger, professionally managed companies.

companies.name: Good Time Home Services
companies.thesis: Family-owned recurring-service candidate with moderate scale
companies.why: Public sources describe a local family-owned business operating since 2006, with residential, commercial/apartment maintenance, preventive maintenance and a broad North Atlanta service area.
companies.counter: Active online scheduling, memberships and broad geography indicate increasing professionalization; ownership names are not yet verified.
companies.next: Identify current owners and team size, isolate recurring apartment/commercial maintenance revenue, and assess customer concentration. Research first; outreach second.

companies.name: Razo Heating & Air Conditioning
companies.thesis: Owner-visible family business with room to grow
companies.why: Family owned by Miguel Razo, with 15+ years of hands-on industry experience and 1,000+ completed residential/commercial jobs. Owner identity and local roots are unusually clear.
companies.counter: The operating company may be materially younger than the owner's industry experience; scale could be too small for the target acquisition economics.
companies.next: Verify entity formation date, revenue proxy, technician/truck count and maintenance contracts. If scale clears your minimum threshold, this could be a growth-oriented tuck-in rather than a succession acquisition.

companies.name: Climate Heroes Air Conditioning
companies.thesis: Family-owned but growth-oriented and digitally active
companies.why: The company describes itself as family owned, locally trusted and staffed by a team with substantial combined experience; it covers a broad service area and offers 24/7 service, online booking and aggressive promotions.
companies.counter: Combined industry experience is not the same as company age, and its digital/marketing posture looks like a growth company rather than an overlooked legacy operator.
companies.next: Verify entity age, owners and actual operating scale before spending outreach time. Keep as a lower-priority growth/tuck-in candidate.

companies.name: PG Heating & Air
companies.why: Local family-owned HVAC contractor with residential/commercial coverage and 24/7 service. One public page says more than seven years of experience, while another emphasizes 50+ years combined team experience.
companies.counter: This appears younger than the original V2 record implied and is likely not a classic succession target.
companies.next: Verify entity start date, owner identity, team size and customer base. Consider only as a small growth tuck-in if financial scale works.

companies.name: PV Heating, Cooling & Plumbing
companies.why: Family owned since 2008 by three brothers and now a sophisticated full-service home-comfort company with HVAC/plumbing, online booking, advanced diagnostics, thousands of reviews and thousands of plan members.
companies.counter: The company is digitally sophisticated, multi-service and visibly growth-oriented—the opposite of the hidden-owner/under-marketed target thesis.
companies.next: Remove from first-wave acquisition outreach. Retain as an operating benchmark for membership programs, training, cross-sell and digital execution.

companies.name: Staton Heating & Air
companies.why: Family owned since 1972 and currently run by the next generation under Mark Staton. It has 875+ Google reviews, online booking, financing, multiple maintenance tiers, certifications and a broad service footprint.
companies.counter: Next-generation leadership and advanced recurring-revenue/digital systems substantially weaken the succession-gap thesis.
companies.next: Do not lead with acquisition outreach. Use Staton as a benchmark for recurring maintenance, financing, brand/review density and professionalization; revisit only if public ownership objectives change.

companies.name: Estes Services
companies.why: Family owned since 1949, now third generation, nearly 200 team members according to its anniversary material, mature maintenance memberships, HVAC/plumbing/electrical and highly sophisticated operations.
companies.counter: Estes explicitly says it has refused consolidator sale attempts and is committed to remaining independent; it also has visible next-generation leadership.
companies.next: Remove from acquisition prospecting. Study as a best-in-class independent benchmark for succession, memberships, diversification, training and brand durability.

companies.name: Moncrief Heating & Air Conditioning
companies.why: Moncrief announced that Ace Hardware acquired the company in July 2023. The family continues to manage it, but it is no longer an independent off-market acquisition target.
companies.counter: None for the current thesis; ownership status disqualifies it.
companies.next: Remove from target list and tag as acquired/strategic-owner. Keep only as a comparable transaction/market-consolidation reference.

companies.name: Fox Pros HVAC
companies.why: BBB says the business began in March 2025 and identifies Cody Fox as owner. The company website says Cody and John have long industry experience, but that is not the same as the operating company's age.
companies.counter: It may become an attractive growth company, but it is not an established legacy/succession candidate today.
companies.next: Correct the V2 start date, remove from succession-focused ranking and place on a separate emerging-growth watchlist.

companies.name: Cool Season Heating & Cooling
companies.thesis: Younger family business with visible next-gen involvement
companies.why: The existing research identified family ownership and next-generation involvement in marketing/operations. That is more consistent with a developing family enterprise than an unresolved succession gap.
companies.counter: Younger company and visible family operating involvement reduce urgency for the acquisition thesis.
companies.next: Verify entity age, owners, technician count and revenue scale; keep as watchlist rather than first-wave outreach.

companies.name: Knox Heating and Air Conditioning
companies.why: The current database originates from a Forsyth County business-license record, which confirms local operating presence but is insufficient to establish quality, longevity, scale or ownership depth.
companies.counter: The prior score was based on too little evidence.
companies.next: Do not outreach yet. Resolve active entity, website, license, owner, reviews, team/fleet and years in business first; only then assign an acquisition score.

companies.name: A&K Service Heating & Cooling
companies.thesis: Promising legacy signal but source quality insufficient
companies.why: The prior page cited a local directory for 30+ years in business and founder experience, which is interesting but not strong enough evidence for an A-level acquisition recommendation.
companies.counter: Ownership, legal entity, current scale, website and operating continuity need authoritative verification.
companies.next: Verify Georgia entity/conditioned-air license, official website, current owner, review footprint, technicians and service agreements before any outreach.
